claim_title: Three of five exercises nonclustered indexes are leading-column redundant
corrected_severity: NONE (not a finding — no redundancy exists)
summary: The claim's central premise is false. No nonclustered index on dbo.exercises is a leading-column prefix of any other. The 'strict prefix' assertions mis-order key columns: e.g. idx_exercises_lesson_order is (lesson_id, order_index) while idx_exercises_lesson_type_order is (lesson_id, exercise_type, order_index) — the second column differs (order_index vs exercise_type), so it is NOT a prefix. A pairwise prefix test over the live catalogs returns zero rows. Forced-index plans prove each index is independently necessary. Sizes/rows/fragmentation are real but were quoted to support a false structural conclusion.

fragmentation_pct.note: Claim said 'all fragmentation < 11%' — true (max 10.92%). This part is accurate but irrelevant to the redundancy claim.

reproducible_evidence.included_columns_note: idx_exercises_lesson_type_order carries included (non-key) columns difficulty and correct_answer. These do not affect leading-column prefix analysis but do mean it is wider than a pure key prefix would be.

refutation_1_no_prefix_relation_exists.method: Pairwise test over sys.indexes/sys.index_columns: for every ordered pair (a,b) of nonclustered indexes, test whether b.keycols starts with a.keycols + ',' (true leading prefix) or equals it.
refutation_1_no_prefix_relation_exists.sql: WITH k AS (SELECT i.name idx, ic.key_ordinal ord, c.name col FROM sys.indexes i JOIN sys.index_columns ic ON ic.object_id=i.object_id AND ic.index_id=i.index_id AND ic.is_included_column=0 JOIN sys.columns c ON c.object_id=ic.object_id AND c.column_id=ic.column_id WHERE i.object_id=OBJECT_ID('exercises') AND i.type=2), v AS (SELECT idx, STRING_AGG(col,',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ord) keycols FROM k GROUP BY idx) SELECT a.idx, b.idx, a.keycols, b.keycols FROM v a JOIN v b ON a.idx<>b.idx WHERE b.keycols LIKE a.keycols + ',%' OR b.keycols = a.keycols
refutation_1_no_prefix_relation_exists.conclusion: No index is a prefix of, or identical to, any other. The claim's three 'strict prefix' relations are all structurally false.

refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.claim: idx_exercises_lesson_order (lesson_id, order_index) is a strict prefix of idx_exercises_lesson_type_order (lesson_id, exercise_type, order_index)
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.actual: FALSE. Position 2 differs: order_index vs exercise_type. A prefix requires lesson_id, order_index to be the FIRST two keys of the other; the other's second key is exercise_type, not order_index.
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.proof: Forced plan SELECT ... WITH (INDEX(idx_exercises_lesson_type_order)) WHERE lesson_id=1 ORDER BY order_index ASC yields 'Sort(ORDER BY order_index ASC) |-- Index Seek(...idx_exercises_lesson_type_order..., SEEK lesson_id=1) ORDERED FORWARD'. The extra Sort means the covering index cannot return rows in order_index order; the dedicated index is required to avoid the sort.

refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.claim: idx_exercises_type (exercise_type) is a prefix of idx_exercises_lesson_type_order
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.actual: FALSE. idx_exercises_lesson_type_order's LEADING column is lesson_id, not exercise_type. exercise_type is the SECOND key. A leading-column prefix must start at column 1.
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.proof: Forced plan SELECT ... WITH (INDEX(idx_exercises_lesson_type_order)) WHERE exercise_type='MULTIPLE_CHOICE' yields an Index SCAN with residual predicate, not a seek. IO: natural (idx_exercises_type) = 142 logical reads; forced onto idx_exercises_lesson_type_order = 458 logical reads. 3.2x worse.

refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.claim: idx_exercises_lesson_order is a prefix of IX_exercises_lesson_type_diff_order (lesson_id, exercise_type, difficulty, order_index)
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.actual: FALSE. Same second-column mismatch: order_index vs exercise_type.
refutation_2_claimed_pairs_are_wrong.proof: Same as pair 1 — the diff_order index orders by exercise_type then difficulty before order_index, so lesson+order_index reads are not covered.

refutation_3_optimizer_uses_each_index_i.method: SET SHOWPLAN_TEXT ON for the real repository query shapes, plus sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats on the live instance.

plans.query: WHERE lesson_id=1 ORDER BY order_index ASC  (repo: findByLessonIdOrderByOrderIndexAsc, ExerciseRepository.java:23-24)
plans.op: Index Seek, ORDERED FORWARD, no Sort

plans.query: WHERE exercise_type='MULTIPLE_CHOICE'  (repo: findAdminPage type filter, ExerciseRepository.java:50)
WHERE lesson_id=1 AND exercise_type='MULTIPLE_CHOICE' ORDER BY order_index ASC  (repo: findByLessonIdAndExerciseTypeOrderByOrderIndexAsc, line 44)
plans.op: Index Seek, ORDERED FORWARD, no Sort

plans.query: WHERE lesson_id=1 AND difficulty='EASY' ORDER BY order_index ASC  (repo: findByLessonIdAndDifficultyOrderByOrderIndexAsc, line 45)

refutation_3_optimizer_uses_each_index_i.conclusion: Each of the five nonclustered indexes is exercised by the optimizer for a distinct query shape. None is dead weight.

refutation_4_io_measurements.note: Forcing the 'redundant' index's would-be cover onto either query is measurably worse (more reads and/or an added Sort), so the claim's premise that these are droppable is contradicted by execution, not just by catalog structure.

probe_artefact_check.notes: Sizes, row count (43,735) and fragmentation figures in the claim are genuine live readings — the claim is not fabricated at the data level. The error is analytical: the author read key-column lists and inferred prefix relations without checking column positions. No 429 / scrollbar / redirect artefacts apply (this is a SQL-layer claim).

answers_to_posed_questions.is_evidence_real_or_artefact: The raw numbers are real (reproduced exactly), but the evidence does not support the conclusion; the three prefix relations are false.
answers_to_posed_questions.is_severity_justified: No — LOW is unjustified. There is no redundancy, so there is no cleanup candidate and no finding at all. Corrected severity: NONE.
answers_to_posed_questions.is_this_correct_behaviour: Yes. Five distinct key compositions serving five distinct query shapes (lesson+order, type-only, lesson+type+order, lesson+difficulty+order, lesson+type+difficulty+order) is intentional, correct schema design, not a defect.
